newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOBSLEIGH-SWISS REBOUND TO TAKE FOUR-MAN TITLE.
newsitem.headline: BOBSLEIGH-SWISS REBOUND TO TAKE FOUR-MAN TITLE.

text.p: Reto Goetschi of Switzerland won the season's final World Cup four-man bobsleigh event on Wednesday while team mate Marcel Rohner took the overall four-man title with a third-place finish.

Italy's Guenther Huber won the combined title ahead of Brian Shimer of the United States, who was second on the 1,360-metre Spiral track where bob and luge events will be held at next year's Nagano Winter Olympics.

The Swiss victories came just a day after bobsleigh officials upheld the disqualifications of medallists Goetschi, Rohner and fellow Swiss Christian Reich at the four-man world championships more than three weeks ago in St. Moritz, Switzerland.
All three were ruled to have used three-piece screwed axels prohibited under international rules.
Reverting to sleds with fixed axels, the Swiss dominated the 15-curve track which has been widely praised by athletes during its World Cup debut.
Reich's 10th-place finish made Switzerland the only nation to place three sleds in the top 10.
"It was great for us because we proved that we are good racers even with regular bobs," said Goetschi, who had the day's two fastest runs to finish in a combined time of one minute 47.02 seconds.
"But I would like to emphasise that I don't think we had an advantage with those other bobs," said the two-man silver medallist at the Lillehammer Olympics.
Shimer, winner of Tuesday's make-up World Cup race, was 0.41 seconds behind Goetschi.
Rohner, third in 1:47.55, topped the four-man standings with 207 points, ahead of Germany's Wolfgang Hoppe, who had 195, and Huber with 190.
Huber, who finished second in the two-man rankings, took the combined title with 414 points. Shimer placed second with 362 points, followed by Canada's Pierre Lueders with 349. Rohner was fourth.
"We needed this," said Swiss Bobsleigh Federation president Giancarlo Torriani. "We showed that we can ride as well on the old axel."

Torriani said the Swiss would be unable to submit an appeal against their disqualifications to the international sports tribunal in Lausanne, Switzerland, as intended, because the International Bobsleigh Federation was not a member.
But Torriani said he would consult a lawyer about launching civil action when he returned to Switzerland on Monday.
